desc: Ideation: identified and justified the forced-edge characterization: an edge is used iff its side size is not divisible by K, and sufficiency is equivalent to the used-edge subgraph being disjoint paths of K vertices.

Implement the forced-edge modulo-cut solution in Python: read N,K, set M=N*K, build adjacency; iterative DFS/BFS from 1 to get tree_parent and order; compute subtree sizes bottom-up; for each v=2..M, if subtree_size[v] % K != 0 then union v with tree_parent[v] in a DSU and increment used-degree of both endpoints; finally print Yes iff all used-degrees are <=2 and for every vertex v the DSU component size of find(v) is exactly K (this naturally handles K=1); use sys.stdin.buffer and a main guard, and do not hardcode samples.
Verify the implementation on the two samples and edge cases (M=1, K=1, N=1 with path/star, K=M, and small random trees against brute force if feasible).
